Bound how long a call can run

Source: R/timeout_method.R, R/timeout.R
timeout.Rd

Decorator that stops a single call after seconds and signals a fnware_timeout_error. Unlike stop_after_delay(), which only checks between attempts, it bounds the call itself.

Usage

timeout_r()

timeout(f, seconds, method = timeout_r())

timeout_remaining()

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

seconds

Time limit for one call, in seconds. A number greater than 0.

method

How to enforce the limit: a timeout method such as timeout_r(). See timeout_fn() to write your own.

Value

timeout() returns a decorator, timeout_r() a timeout method and timeout_remaining() a number of seconds.

Details

The condition inherits from error, so retry_if_error() retries it and circuit_breaker() counts it as a failure. It records the limit in $limit and the function name in $fn. Stack timeout() inside retry() so each attempt is capped. Outside retry() the limit is already spent when the error is caught, so later attempts run unbounded.

Timeouts can nest. The soonest active deadline always applies, so an inner timeout never outlasts an outer one. timeout_remaining() returns the seconds left before that deadline, or Inf outside any timeout(), so you can pass the budget to a library with its own timeout. It does not see deadlines in other R processes unless a method passes one on, see timeout_fn().

For functions that return a promise, use async_timeout().

Limitations

timeout_r() uses setTimeLimit(), which R only checks between R expressions. It cannot interrupt compiled code that never checks for interrupts (many blocking network and database calls), or a single long Sys.sleep(). For those, pass timeout_remaining() to a native timeout or use a process-based method. Code that catches every error around the slow part will also catch the time limit error.

Timeout methods

method decides how the limit is enforced. timeout_r() is the only built-in method. To write your own, see timeout_fn().

Examples

# A loop of short steps is interrupted between steps
slow <- function() {
  for (i in 1:100) Sys.sleep(0.05)
  "done"
}
f := timeout(0.2) %@% slow
try(f())
#> Error : `f` timed out: it did not finish within 0.2 seconds.

# Each attempt is capped, and a timeout is retried
attempts <- 0
flaky := retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(3)) %@%
  timeout(0.2) %@%
  function() {
    attempts <<- attempts + 1
    if (attempts < 3) slow() else "worked"
  }
flaky()
#> [1] "worked"

# Pass the remaining budget on
budget := timeout(10) %@% function() timeout_remaining()
budget()
#> [1] 10
